name: @w6w-apps/vero
description: Identify, track, tag, alias, delete, and subscribe/unsubscribe users via Vero's Track API.

w6w.longDescription:
Vero's Track API is the write side of customer data for its customer-engagement platform — creating and updating user profiles, recording events, editing tags, changing (aliasing) a user's identifier, deleting a user outright, and globally subscribing or unsubscribing a user from email. This app implements exactly that surface, the seven verbs that have been stable and unchanged since before 2016.

Vero exposes a second, separate REST surface — the Campaigns API — for managing broadcasts, journeys and preference-center topics. This app deliberately does not call it: it is a public preview that Vero grants access to only on request (a distinct API key most connections will not have), and its resource schemas (Broadcast, Journey, Topic, and their nested Message/Content children) are a different, much larger surface than the stable Track API this app targets. Noted here rather than silently dropped.

A few operations carry consequences worth knowing: deleting a user is permanent and not recoverable, aliasing (reidentifying) a user retargets their id so a retry against the old id no longer resolves, and Vero automatically deduplicates identical Track Event calls (same auth token, event name, identity and data) within a five-minute window, so a host retry converges on the original event rather than double-firing it.
